title: A star formation laboratory
caption: The dwarf galaxy NGC 4214, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4214 · constellation Canes Venatici · about 10 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration. Acknowledgment: R. O’Connell (University of Virginia) and the WFC3 Scientific Oversight Committee

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A huge glowing cloud of hydrogen gas dominates much of this galaxy, and at its centre sits a heart-shaped hollow. This is NGC 4214, pictured with Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, which was the telescope's newest camera when the image was made.

The glowing cloud is a nursery where new stars are forming, which makes the galaxy an ideal place to study how stars are born and how they evolve. Inside the heart-shaped cavity is a large cluster of massive young stars, with temperatures from 10 000 to 50 000 degrees Celsius.

Those stars carved the hollow themselves. Their strong stellar winds, streams of particles blowing off their surfaces, pushed the gas outward into a bubble. That has a side effect: with the gas cleared away, the raw material for making more stars is gone, so the same winds that shaped the heart are also slowing further star birth nearby.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.54 x 2.16 arcminutes) and distance (10 million light years), the frame spans roughly 7,400 × 6,300 light-years. Its light set out about 10 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using filters from the ultraviolet through visible light to the near-infrared, including ones tuned to glowing hydrogen and oxygen. The packet does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, and the galaxy is far too faint to see in this detail without a large telescope.

explore: NGC 4214 is a dwarf galaxy, much smaller than the Milky Way, lying about 10 million light-years away in the constellation Canes Venatici.
alt: A galaxy dominated by a glowing cloud of gas with a heart-shaped hollow at its centre.
